chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Recording 'Yacht Club Swing' with the Claude Hopkins band
summary: He was called back to Fats eventually, but on a recording date with Hopkins he played first trumpet, soloed, sang, and Hopkins recorded his tune 'Yacht Club Swing'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: And how did he get you?
Well, they called me there, and they told me to get back to the band.
How long were you with Claude? Let's put it that way.

Well I wasn't very happy. Let's see, how many months did that run into? Because after Robertson came back we did a few things, quite a few things, got to go, and have another job, I had to stay with him. Until I got -- you know -- got a chance to get back with Fats.
Exactly how many months, or weeks, or this -- I rightly -- I don't --
Who was in the band then? Was Ed Hall in that band?

No. No, no. I didn't work in that band with Ed. Ed had left before I ever joined him. And I joined -- I joined them -- that was quite a while after he left. I stayed with the group because I did a recording date with Claude Hopkins. He did my tune, for one thing, 'Yacht Club Swing.'

Yeah, and I went in there and I played first trumpet for him, because -- I'm trying to think, who was his first trumpet? Who left? When I came in. Well, on some of the recording dates I played, it was that way, I played first because I was a soloist, and sang a couple of things with them, and played -- you know.
